ANALYSIS: The existing translation correctly captures the individual meanings of the Sanskrit words but suffers from ambiguous word order and unclear syntactic relation. “Sārāt” (from the essence) should directly modify “trikabhedam” (threefold distinction), indicating the source of the distinction. In the existing version, “from the essence” is placed at the end, making it appear to modify “classification of essences” rather than “threefold distinction”. The adverb “aśeṣeṇa” (completely) can be rendered as an adjective (“complete”) or adverb (“in its entirety”); both are acceptable, but the relation should be clear. The phrase “sāravibhāgaśaḥ” (according to the classification of essences) provides the manner and is correctly translated.

CORRECTED: “The complete threefold distinction from the essence, according to the classification of essences.” (Alternatively: “The threefold distinction in its entirety from the essence, according to the classification of essences.”)
